title: Colours of some cobalt(III) complexes
body: A student studies a set of octahedral cobalt(III) complexes. In each, Co³⁺ (a 3d⁶ ion) is surrounded by six ligands, and the five d orbitals split into a lower t₂g set and a higher eg set separated by the crystal field splitting energy, Δo. A complex absorbs light whose energy matches an electronic transition and shows the complementary colour. The energy of a photon is inversely proportional to its wavelength. The student records these data: [Co(NH₃)₅(H₂O)]³⁺ absorbs at 500 nm (blue-green) and appears red; [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ absorbs at 475 nm (blue) and appears yellow-orange; [Co(CN)₆]³⁻ absorbs at 310 nm (ultraviolet) and appears pale yellow. The student also recalls the spectrochemical series, in which H₂O < NH₃ < CN⁻ in field strength.
